title: Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study

ai_method: Continual learning sequentially retrains an adult endotracheal-tube model at participating neonatal units.
study_summary: The retrospective international evaluation improves landmark error relative to adult-only and local fine-tuning models at most sites. Raw images cannot be redistributed; trained weights are shared.

title: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer

ai_method: A trained random-forest classifier applied to deep-sequenced plasma cfDNA.
study_summary: Maps subtype-specific therapeutic-resistance and targetable alterations in a large metastatic cohort. The learned subtype assignments support cohort characterization and trial planning, not evidence that model-guided treatment improves survival.

title: Low-input deep learning platform for citrullinated peptide identification, autoantigen discovery and rheumatoid arthritis treatment stratification
research_problem: Improve citrullinated-peptide discovery and treatment stratification in rheumatoid arthritis.
ai_method: Iseq-Cit proteomics is combined with a bidirectional gated recurrent unit and clinical-proteomic prediction models.
study_summary: Longitudinal profiles are linked to RA development and severity. External ELISA experiments report 84.2% accuracy for peptide-serum reactivity, with 19 diagnostic candidates nominated. Peptides are a different unit from patients.

title: An ophthalmic video foundation model for surgical recognition and navigation with wet-lab porcine eye validation
research_problem: Make ophthalmic video models practical for real-time surgical recognition and navigation.
ai_method: OVFM uses self-supervised video-transformer pretraining and knowledge distillation for deployment.
study_summary: The distilled model is deployed on surgical microscopes. Ten surgeons perform cataract procedures on wet-lab porcine eyes, with improved performance and narrower experience gaps. This is not a patient surgical trial.

title: Confounding factors and biases abound when predicting molecular biomarkers from histological images
research_problem: Determine whether histology-based biomarker models learn confounded clinicopathological signals.
ai_method: Statistical dependency analyses and deep-learning audits across cancer types, cohorts and modelling approaches.
study_summary: Dependencies between biomarkers and features such as tumour grade can inflate or alter apparent prediction performance. Some gains beyond routine pathology are modest; the authors caution against replacing molecular assays.
